\begin{abstract}
We study how default contribution rates interact with present bias in a field experiment with 1,200 employees. Automatic enrollment reduces the share of employees who save nothing by 23\% relative to the control group. A present-bias parameter of $\beta = 0.82$ explains the pattern. We discuss implications for the design of retirement plans.
\end{abstract}

\noindent JEL codes: D15, D91, G51

\noindent Keywords: defaults, present bias, retirement saving, field experiment
